105.canonical: Design distributed systems for network reality rather than as if they were a single in-process application: explicitly counter the fallacies of distributed computing — the network is unreliable (use timeouts/circuit breakers), latency is non-zero (track average and tail latency), bandwidth is finite (minimize data, avoid stamp coupling), the network is insecure (secure every endpoint), the topology changes, and platforms are heterogeneous.

108.canonical: Never treat a common data representation as common semantics: integrating heterogeneous systems brings semantic and conceptual dissonance where the same field means different things across divisions, so explicitly resolve semantic differences and plan reconciliation as a combined business and technical task rather than assuming shared meaning.

116.canonical: Design every Aggregator around three explicit decisions — correlation (by a unique per-transaction identifier rather than a shared attribute), a completeness condition, and an aggregation algorithm — keeping the aggregation logic in strongly-typed domain objects independent of the messaging API.

120.canonical: Use a Message Filter so each system receives only the messages matching its criteria, dropping unwanted messages from a channel; run it stateless for parallelism or stateful when it must remember history such as for de-duplication.

121.canonical: Prefer coarse-grained, self-contained remote interfaces over fine-grained ones — bundling work into fewer, bulkier calls to minimize round trips, synchronization overhead, and coupling — keeping this remote interface distinct from a fine-grained local interface, while balancing against interfaces so coarse they limit flexibility.

126.canonical: Use asynchronous, queue-based pipelines to raise throughput by decoupling producer and consumer: parallelize the slowest stage with Competing Consumers on a Point-to-Point Channel, parallelize only stateless filters, and preserve ordering when it is critical with a single instance, a Resequencer, or a correlation identifier to match out-of-order results.

127.canonical: Make production filters transactional so a failure before the output is sent does not lose the message: open a transaction before consuming the input and commit only after publishing the output, aborting on any exception to roll back both and return the input to the queue.

136.canonical: On a Publish-Subscribe Channel a subscriber only receives messages published while it is actively subscribed, so subscribe before messages of interest are published and use a Durable Subscriber when an observer must receive messages published while it was temporarily disconnected.

138.canonical: Make communication two-way with a pair of Request-Reply messages: have the requestor specify a Return Address in the request header so the replier need not hard-code channels, and carry a Correlation Identifier (set to the request's message ID) on the reply so the requestor can match each reply to its request.
